items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: It was Tony Williams’ Original Lifetime and he had discovered John McLaughlin... And it was Tony and John and Larry Young.

ctx.x: Right. Well you lived in Boston, grew up in Boston, and did you have a musical family? Because your brother is a musician also.

My parents loved music pretty much. They’re both fans. My dad had a nice singing voice and played the violin when he was a kid. But they weren’t involved with music at all. They just loved it. And my brother and I, Tony, picked up on that I guess. And also the © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

school system we went to in Brookline had a great music department and some really good teachers in the system, which, that’s invaluable. That’s so great because it inspires kids. If it’s in you at all they’ll just bring it out, they’ll give you an opening, you go into the opening and that’s it. And here we are. Where we went wrong, as musicians.
